stem.en: A teacher strikes a tuning fork on a rubber pad and holds it by the stem. You hear a note. She strikes it again, but this time holds it tightly by one prong. What happens to the sound?

text.en: The sound becomes louder, because the hand keeps feeding fresh movement into the fork.
There is no change, because the stem and the prong are the same single piece of metal.
The sound stops, because only the stem can carry the sound into the air.
The sound stops, because a hand on a prong stops that prong from moving to and fro.

explanation.en: A hand on a prong holds that prong still, so the fork cannot vibrate, and the sound stops. That is why you hold a tuning fork by its stem: the prongs stay free to vibrate.

hints.en: What does a hand do to a part it holds tightly?
The prongs are the parts that vibrate. The stem is only a handle.
